messages:
pagerduty-bot: SEV2 alert - high error rate for /generate endpoints, increased 5xxs and OOM traces. Pager: serving-runtime-team oncall
alex.sre: seeing lots of kernel OOM messages on node-gpu-17, kubelet eviction of pods due to ephemeral storage pressure. Symptoms: model serving containers crash with CUDA init errors after restart.
maya.prodeng: confirmed. Grafana shows disk free on /var/lib/kubelet/pods/tmp (tmpfs) dropping to < 30MB on node-gpu-17 and node-gpu-12. Error burst started ~8m ago. Customer-facing error spike ~6m.
chao.runtime: logs from model-server show repeated failed mmap calls then CUDA driver errors: 'CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY' and then 'failed to load shard: io error'. Looks like KV cache writes failing when disk full.
sarah.support: support queue showing multiple customers with timeouts; one user reported 500s in EU region. Need to notify customer-impact channel after quick assessment.
oncall: I'm on it. Will run a quick node check and try to reclaim ephemeral. Any non-invasive mitigations first.
alex.sre: trying to SSH node-gpu-17 to inspect ephemeral usage. Running du on modelcache and /var/log. Suspect log backlog from crash loops plus large model shard writes to emptyDir.
alex.sre: output:
```
root@node-gpu-17: du -sh /var/lib/kubelet/pods/* | sort -hr | head -n 10
2.3G /var/lib/kubelet/pods/abcd-1234/modelcache
1.2G /var/lib/kubelet/pods/efgh-5678/containers/logs
512M /var/lib/kubelet/pods/ijkl-9012/checkpoints
```
chao.runtime: model cache is using a lot of tmp storage. For now we can remove old model shards and let the runtime stream from S3 as a fallback. But need to throttle traffic to avoid thundering herd.
maya.prodeng: propose immediate steps: 1) cordon node-gpu-17 2) scale down model-server replica on that node (kubectl drain with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data?) 3) remove stale logs and old cache files 4) restart kubelet if needed.
oncall: caution on --delete-local-data. That can drop local checkpoints. Prefer to delete only log files and oldest cache shards. I can run targeted rm on files >30d and rotate.
alex.sre: I'm going to run `journalctl --vacuum-time=2d` and rotate logs on the node. Also truncating container logs with: `truncate -s 0 /var/log/pods/*/*.log` for the crash-looping pods.
oncall: starting truncation now. tagging pods to avoid immediate reschedule onto same node.
chao.runtime: while that runs, I’ll update runtime config to reduce cache write aggressiveness and enable smaller shard size for fallback variant on the router so new pods use a lighter cache profile.
sarah.support: drafting a short customer message: 'We are investigating increased 5xxs in EU. Working on storage pressure on a small subset of GPU nodes; mitigation in progress. We will update in 30 minutes.' Want to post after we confirm impact window.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy 2026.03.15-rollback triggered for model-bert-large due to high errors. Canary count reduced from 20 -> 5.
alex.sre: truncation done, removed ~1.4G of logs. Freed ~1.7G after journal vacuum. Model cache still ~1.8G.
chao.runtime: next step: move modelcache dir to hostPath backed on ephemeral SSD with more space. We can patch pod spec to mount /mnt/ssd/modelcache and rsync files over, then update symlink. Quick plan:
```
kubectl -n inference exec -it pod/model-123 -- bash -c '\
  mkdir -p /mnt/ssd/modelcache && rsync -a /var/tmp/modelcache/ /mnt/ssd/modelcache/ && ln -sfn /mnt/ssd/modelcache /var/tmp/modelcache'
```
Note: this requires hostPath available on node. If not, we fallback to removing oldest shards and letting fetch-from-s3.
maya.prodeng: can we also enable fallback routing to model-medium for new requests for 15m window? That will lower memory/disk use and reduce errors.
chao.runtime: already added a temporary routing rule: traffic to /generate -> model-medium for 20% of requests, and 100% for requests arriving to affected nodes. Should throttle retries at the client side as well.
oncall: I've cordoned node-gpu-17 to prevent new scheduling. Draining would evict data; I'm leaving pods but marked unschedulable.
alex.sre: after freeing space, observed one runtime successfully restart and serve without immediate CUDA error. However a second pod still fails with 'failed to allocate megacache region'. Could be leftover leak in runtime memory -> will restart runtime process gracefully.
chao.runtime: rolling restart of model-server on node-gpu-17 in progress with backoff policy 30s. Also enabling kv-cache compaction: `kvctl compact --threshold 0.5` on affected pods.
sarah.support: posted initial customer note to status page and support queue. Message ID: status-8472. Customers with SLA flagged were DM'd by support.
alex.sre: monitoring latencies and 5xx rates. Error rate dropped from 7% -> 2% after initial frees and routing change.
oncall: handing off to night oncall in 20 minutes. Will document steps taken and open a follow-up ticket to revisit modelcache placement and log rotation policies.
maya.prodeng: created follow-up ticket INF-7721 with recommended mitigations: 1) move modelcache to hostPath on GPU nodes, 2) set logrotate for containers to 10MB max, 3) add soft eviction threshold for emptyDir usage, 4) add monitoring alert for tmpfs < 200MB.
chao.runtime: also recommending runtime change: write-through to S3 for shards > 256MB and lazy eviction policy.
oncall: handing over to oncall (night): please monitor node-gpu-17 and node-gpu-12, uncordon only after we confirm stable memory and no more OOMs for 15m.
sarah.support: updating customers: 'Issue reduced; mitigation continues. We'll confirm full recovery by 15:45 UTC or earlier.'
oncall: oncall ack. Leaving notes: truncated logs, journal vacuum, moved partial cache to ssd, added routing fallback, cordoned node. Escalation if >10% 5xx returns.
alex.sre: closing real-time loop here. Will join postmortem call if needed. :thumbsup:
pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged and marked in progress. Severity remains SEV2.
